items.prompt: Improve this description: 'The park was good.' Write a 2-sentence description using at least 3 specific details.
items.answer: Example: 'The park had a wooden bridge over a sparkling pond, and the air smelled like fresh-cut grass. Children chased each other around a tall oak tree while ducks quacked at the water's edge.'

steps: Replace 'good' with specific details.
Add visual details (wooden bridge, sparkling pond, tall oak tree).
Add sensory details (smell of grass, sound of ducks quacking).
Add action (children playing) to make the scene vivid.

items.prompt:
A student describes a football game: 'My team won. It was exciting.' Which of the following additions would make the description MOST effective?
A) 'I wear a blue jersey.'
B) 'With one second left on the clock, my teammate kicked the ball and it sailed through the goalposts. Everyone in the stands jumped up and screamed.'
items.answer: B) 'With one second left on the clock, my teammate kicked the ball and it sailed through the goalposts. Everyone in the stands jumped up and screamed.'

steps: Option A tells about the jersey — marginally relevant, but not about the exciting moment.
Option B adds a specific, climactic moment (last second, the kick, the crowd's reaction) — this is vivid and directly relevant to why the game was exciting.

items.prompt:
Which description of a classroom gives the BEST relevant details?
A) 'The classroom has many things in it.'
B) 'The classroom has a reading rug covered in star patterns, colorful word charts hanging on the walls, and a fish tank that hums quietly near the window.'
items.answer: B) 'The classroom has a reading rug covered in star patterns, colorful word charts hanging on the walls, and a fish tank that hums quietly near the window.'

steps: Option A is vague ('many things'). Option B names specific objects with specific details (star patterns, colorful, quietly humming fish tank).

items.prompt:
Describe the feeling of being happy using specific details — not just the word 'happy.'
A) 'I felt really happy.'
B) 'My chest felt warm and light, I could not stop grinning, and I wanted to dance around the room.'
items.answer: B) 'My chest felt warm and light, I could not stop grinning, and I wanted to dance around the room.'

steps: Option A just labels the feeling ('happy').
Option B shows the physical and behavioral signs of happiness — much more vivid and expressive.
Good descriptions SHOW feelings through actions and sensations.

items.prompt:
Which detail is NOT relevant when describing a visit to the beach?
A) 'The sand was so hot it burned through my flip-flops.'
B) 'My uncle lives in Ohio.'
C) 'The ocean waves crashed loudly and sent white foam running over my feet.'

steps: Options A and C both describe sensory experiences at the beach — highly relevant.
Option B is about where the uncle lives — completely unrelated to the beach visit.

items.prompt: A student describes her favorite toy: 'It is a stuffed bear. It is brown. It is soft. I like it.' How could she express her ideas AND feelings more clearly in one or two sentences?
items.answer: Example: 'My stuffed bear is small and light brown with a button nose, and its fur is so soft I cuddle it every night before I fall asleep. It makes me feel safe and cozy.'

steps: Combine the separate observations into flowing sentences.
Add a specific physical detail (button nose).
Add a feeling/emotional detail (makes her feel safe and cozy).
Show what she does with it (cuddling at night) to illustrate her feelings.

items.prompt:
Which description of an event best expresses both what happened AND how the speaker felt?
A) 'I fell off my bike. It was bad.'
B) 'I hit a bump on my bike and flew over the handlebars, scraping both knees. My eyes filled with tears, but I got back on and rode all the way home.'
items.answer: B) 'I hit a bump on my bike and flew over the handlebars, scraping both knees. My eyes filled with tears, but I got back on and rode all the way home.'

steps: Option A gives minimal detail and a vague feeling ('bad').
Option B describes the event specifically (hit a bump, flew over handlebars, scraped knees) and shows feelings through action (eyes filled with tears, got back on bike).

items.prompt: A student says: 'My grandma is funny.' List TWO specific behaviors or things she could describe to SHOW that her grandma is funny, rather than just saying it.
items.answer: Examples: (1) 'She tells silly jokes at dinner and always gets the punchline wrong — which makes them even funnier.' (2) 'She does silly dances in the kitchen when she thinks no one is watching.'

steps: Instead of labeling grandma as 'funny,' describe what makes her funny.
Specific behavior 1: tells jokes (even if she gets them wrong).
Specific behavior 2: dances in the kitchen when she thinks no one is watching.
Both behaviors show (not tell) that grandma is funny.

items.prompt:
Which pair of sentences uses better descriptive language for a first day of school?
A) 'I was nervous. The school was big.'
B) 'My hands were shaking as I walked into the tall brick building for the first time. The hallway smelled like new crayons and fresh paint.'
items.answer: B) 'My hands were shaking as I walked into the tall brick building for the first time. The hallway smelled like new crayons and fresh paint.'

steps: Option A tells: 'I was nervous' and 'the school was big' — vague.
Option B shows nervousness (shaking hands), describes the building (tall brick), and adds sensory detail (smell of crayons and paint).

items.prompt:
Improve this description with two more relevant details: 'My cat plays a lot.'
Which addition makes the description most relevant and vivid?
A) 'My cat chases a small crinkle ball across the hardwood floor, sliding into the wall and bouncing back.'
B) 'Cats are common pets.'
items.answer: A) 'My cat chases a small crinkle ball across the hardwood floor, sliding into the wall and bouncing back.'

steps: Option A gives a specific, vivid scene of the cat playing (the ball, sliding, bouncing).
Option B is a generic fact about cats in general — not a relevant detail about the speaker's cat.

items.prompt:
Which description includes the MOST specific relevant details about a person?
A) 'She is tall and has hair.'
B) 'She is tall with curly red hair that bounces when she walks, and she always wears a blue backpack with a key chain of a tiny pineapple.'
items.answer: B) 'She is tall with curly red hair that bounces when she walks, and she always wears a blue backpack with a key chain of a tiny pineapple.'

steps: Option B is packed with specific, visual details (curly red hair, bounces when she walks, blue backpack, pineapple key chain). Option A is minimal and vague.

items.prompt:
What is the purpose of including feelings in a description?
A) To show the listener that the event was important to you, making the description more meaningful and vivid.
B) Feelings are not useful in descriptions.
items.answer: A) To show the listener that the event was important to you, making the description more meaningful and vivid.

steps: Feelings add a personal, emotional dimension to a description. They help the listener understand why the event or person mattered, not just what happened.

items.prompt: Describe a fire using ONLY sensory details (sight, sound, smell, feel). Write 2 sentences.
items.answer: Example: 'The fire crackled and popped loudly, shooting orange and yellow sparks up into the dark sky. The smoke smelled sharp and woody, and the heat pressed against my face like an open oven.'

steps: Sound: crackled and popped.
Sight: orange and yellow sparks, dark sky.
Smell: sharp and woody.
Touch/feel: heat pressed against face like an open oven.

items.prompt: A student describes a rainy walk to school: 'My shoes got wet. I was cold.' Add TWO specific details to make this more vivid.
items.answer: Example: 'Rainwater seeped through my sneakers and soaked my socks all the way through. My fingers turned red from the cold, and I could see my breath puffing out in the gray morning air.'

steps: Add specific detail 1 (how shoes got wet): 'Rainwater seeped through my sneakers and soaked my socks.'
Add specific detail 2 (how cold felt): 'Fingers turned red; could see breath in cold air.'

items.prompt:
A student wants to describe her favorite holiday. She includes: what the holiday is, one specific thing she does, one thing she sees, one thing she smells or tastes, and one feeling. Which student followed these guidelines?
A) 'My favorite holiday is Christmas because it is fun.'
B) 'My favorite holiday is Thanksgiving. We always make pumpkin pie that fills the whole house with a warm, spicy smell. The table is covered with golden food, and I feel full and thankful all day.'
items.answer: B) 'My favorite holiday is Thanksgiving. We always make pumpkin pie that fills the whole house with a warm, spicy smell. The table is covered with golden food, and I feel full and thankful all day.'

steps: Holiday named: Thanksgiving.
Action: make pumpkin pie.
Smell: warm, spicy.
Visual: table covered with golden food.
Feeling: full and thankful.
Option B follows all five guidelines. Option A only names the holiday and uses a vague word ('fun').
